items.title: Roswell Rudd interviewed by Monk Rowe, Ellenville, New York, June 23, 1998
items.q: Francesco Landini, some blind Italian composer and his fragments were just all that you knew about him.

ctx.x: No, I had a hard time because improvisation was considered recreational music at Yale. There was no place for it in the curriculum and it was something that you did after dinner in the lounge or the mess hall. So it wasn’t something that was really being encouraged,

you were really being taught, which is kind of hypocritical, as I began to see more and more, that all that music in the library and in all that classical, that western music collection down there, all that stuff came out of improvisation. And yet improvisation wasn’t encouraged. Because we had this wall of notation that was in the way. Books, books, books, books. All this paper, paper, paper, paper. Volumes, volumes, volumes. And you would never guess that on the other side of this was Francesco Landini, some…
Do you have particular favorite recordings of yourself?
